leads.summary: Existing channel-test.sh's strict dev-flow assertion now fails on the new initial sudo command
leads.consequence: The channel test copies the changed entrypoint with /usr/bin/sudo rewritten to mock/sudo (fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh:16-29), and replaces that mock at channel-test.sh:37-47 with a logger that records every command invocation other than -k/-h. On the dev case the new authorize_channel call emits 'sudo	/usr/bin/true' before git/link. The exact multiline assertion at channel-test.sh:178-179 includes lines beginning 'sudo' but expects only git,link,state,refresh,update, so the head test exits 1. Base had no authorization command and satisfies this particular assertion. Update the expected sequence or make it explicitly assert one authorization between confirmation and git.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroborated; published

leads.summary: The exported session marker is not restricted to channel-set callers, so independent refreshes also stop revoking
leads.consequence: A user can start omarchy-refresh-pacman (or omarchy-reinstall-pkgs, which calls it at line 11) with OMARCHY_UPDATE_SUDO_SESSION=1. It immediately shadows the entry, hook-bracketing and EXIT/signal -k with ':'. If an existing same-session sudo timestamp was already valid, the user hook runs with it and the helper leaves it valid on success or error. In particular omarchy-update exports this marker at update:35 to post-update user hooks at update:140; a hook invoking the standalone refresh inherits it, contrary to the still-shipped docs/update-process.md:156 assertion that such calls revoke. Sudo -N does not renew a ticket but does accept a current ticket (sudo 1.9.17p2 src/parse_args.c:431-435 and plugins/sudoers/check.c:165-185,221-223). If the marker is absent or not exactly '1', the existing cold behavior remains. Preserve a separate, authenticated caller boundary, or clear the marker before independent refreshes and keep real cleanup for any failure.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); corroborated; published

leads.summary: The pre-refresh-pacman hook is documented as cold in three places, despite running with a live ticket during a channel switch
leads.consequence: These user-facing/included instructions promise a hook with no reusable sudo authorization; docs/update-process.md explicitly says channel switching runs it 'cold'. New refresh-pacman shadows both revocations on the channel-set marker and channel-set authorizes before refresh, so the hook and its children can use the still-live timestamp via /usr/bin/sudo or via the -N wrapper. The documentation is a security promise that no longer holds, and it may encourage installing unreviewed hook scripts under a false assumption. Update each of the three references to distinguish standalone refresh from channel switch, and do not state the wrapper isolates a currently live ticket.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroborated; published

leads.summary: With sudo's ppid tickets (including no controlling TTY), a parent channel ticket is not shared with child helpers or the keepalive
leads.consequence: For sudoers timestamp_type=ppid, or the default tty type when there is no controlling TTY but askpass or passwordless sudo can authenticate the first command, upstream sudo records the invoking channel shell's PID as the parent of its initial sudo process. Later sudo invoked in refresh-pacman, the no-update wrapper, update-pacman, and the background keepalive has a different parent and does not match that ticket. The first cached privileged operation may prompt again despite one channel authorization, and sudo -n in the keepalive exits at its first wakeup without refreshing the parent's ticket. With no interactive terminal and no askpass on those later calls, the switch can fail. Do not promise one password universally without limiting supported timestamp policy or redesigning the ticket-sharing mechanism. Source proof of the ticket mismatch, no sudo runtime was executed.
leads.triage: Opus report already lists ppid/timeout=0 as untested hypothesis from sudo source; kept only as a Test scope limit, not a finding

leads.summary: Open #13444 conflicts with the new channel handoff and a correct combined handoff breaks channel-test.sh assertions
leads.consequence: #13444 changes the very last line from update -y to update --skip-confirm so a watched channel switch can still offer reboot. Using #13444's own base version with git merge-file against this head produces conflict markers at merged channel-set:198,207, while merged update has no conflicts and understands --skip-confirm. A naive ours-only resolution silently drops #13444's reboot fix; theirs-only drops end_channel_authorization and unset, losing this PR's update handoff boundary. Resolving correctly to 'end_channel_authorization; unset ...; update --skip-confirm' still requires changing channel-test.sh's hard-coded 'update -y' assertions. #13444 is diverged rather than stacked; GitHub calls its mergeability MERGEABLE against quattro, not against this PR. Coordinate the tail resolution and update both tests if both PRs merge.

leads.summary: There is no negative authorization-refusal check in the changed channel boundary suite
leads.consequence: The stub supports SUDO_TEST_SUDO_FAIL=1 (fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh:59-64), but channel-sudo-boundary-test.sh tests failures in pacman, update-system-pkgs, hook and entry -k/-h only. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at b19dfb1, a channel switch asks for one authorization for the switch itself and then hands off to the update's own single authorization. The keepalive refreshes the ticket through long pacman transactions and is stopped before the ticket is revoked at the hand-off. HUP, INT, TERM, step failures, a refused password and `stop_for_older_destination` all exit with the ticket revoked. Standalone `omarchy-refresh-pacman` behaves as before when `OMARCHY_UPDATE_SUDO_SESSION` is unset.

Prompts per switch, from a mock sudo modelled on sudo 1.9.17p2 source (default sudoers, a hook that does not call sudo, no AUR updates):

| Path | quattro 3faafba (switch + update) | b19dfb1 (switch + update) |
|---|---|---|
| stable, rc, edge, leaving dev | 8 + 1 | 1 + 1 |
| dev (fresh clone or existing checkout) | 8 + 1 | 1 + 1 |

The dev counts assume the `~/omarchy` checkout includes this change. The dev path runs refresh-pacman from that checkout, so an older checkout that still revokes on entry would bring per-command prompts back (inferred from source, not run).

Four points follow: an existing test that now fails, a relaxed hook boundary that the docs still describe as cold, a session flag that also applies inside `omarchy update`, and the dev-path ordering.

### `test/shell.d/channel-test.sh` fails on this branch

The dev case exits with `not ok - dev activates the checkout before changing or updating packages` at b19dfb1 and passes at 3faafba. The order check at `test/shell.d/channel-test.sh:178` greps `sudo` lines too, and the new `/usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/true` authorization is now logged first, before `git clone`. Because the file stops at its first failure, the later cases (dev to stable, switching back to dev, channel detection) no longer run.

**Impact:** the focused test for this command fails, and `./test/shell` should fail with it (the full suite was not run). The changed `channel-sudo-boundary-test.sh` passes, so running only that file does not show it.

**Suggested change:** add `sudo\t/usr/bin/true` as the first expected line in that sequence. With only that edit, the whole file passes. If the dev-path reordering below is adopted, the `sudo` line moves after `git clone` instead.

### The `pre-refresh-pacman` hook now runs with a live sudo ticket

During a switch, `omarchy-refresh-pacman` replaces `omarchy_security_revoke_sudo_timestamp` with a no-op (`bin/omarchy-refresh-pacman:24-27`), so the revocations on either side of the hook no longer run:

```text
quattro:   sudo -k -> pre-refresh-pacman hook (no ticket) -> sudo -k -> pacman -Syyuu
b19dfb1:   channel ticket (kept alive every 60 s) -> hook -> pacman -Syyuu -> package swap -> sudo -k -> update
```

In sudo 1.9.17p2, `-N` only stops sudo from updating the ticket. It still uses an existing one (`plugins/sudoers/check.c`, `src/parse_args.c`). In the mock model, a bare `sudo` in the hook (through the no-update wrapper) and an absolute-path `/usr/bin/sudo -n` both succeed without a prompt at b19dfb1. Both needed a password at 3faafba.

The PR body does list the hook among the steps that share the authorization, and this extends the trade-off #13323 made for `post-update`. #13415 asked for that choice to be made explicitly. The new comment understates it, and three documents still describe the old cold boundary:

- `bin/omarchy-refresh-pacman:48-52`: "the wrapper still prevents the hook from caching a credential of its own". That is true for bare `sudo`, but the hook's privileged commands now run without a prompt.
- `docs/update-process.md:273-275`: "Channel switching runs the `pre-refresh-pacman` hook once … cold, behind the no-update wrapper".
- `manual/31-dotfiles.md:46`: "a hook that uses `sudo` needs its own authorization and may ask for your password".
- `default/agents/skills/omarchy/hooks.md:30`: "a detached child left behind by the hook has nothing to wait for". During a switch, a child on the same terminal can use the channel ticket until the hand-off, covering both pacman transactions.

One difference from #13323: `omarchy-update` creates its ticket inside its own `script(1)` pty, but the channel ticket lives on the caller's terminal. Other processes in that terminal session can also use it while the switch runs.

**Impact:** hook authors and users relying on the documented cold boundary get a different privilege model during channel switches than the docs describe.

**Suggested change:** state the relaxation plainly in the comment at `bin/omarchy-refresh-pacman:48-52`, and update the three documents to distinguish a standalone refresh from a channel switch.

### `OMARCHY_UPDATE_SUDO_SESSION=1` also disables refresh-pacman's revocations inside `omarchy update`

`bin/omarchy-update:35` already exports `OMARCHY_UPDATE_SUDO_SESSION=1` for the whole update. With this PR, an `omarchy-refresh-pacman` run from a post-update hook matches the same check and drops every revocation, not just the channel case:

| Nested refresh from a post-update hook (mock model) | 3faafba | b19dfb1 |
|---|---|---|
| `sudo -k` during the refresh | 4 | 0 |
| Ticket at its `pre-refresh-pacman` hook | none | live |
| Ticket after the refresh returns | revoked | live |

**Impact:** this contradicts `docs/update-process.md:156` ("Standalone commands that keep their own cold boundary, such as `omarchy-refresh-pacman`, still revoke if a post-update hook calls them"). The flag is also an ordinary inherited variable. These entrypoints strip shell-startup variables such as `BASH_ENV` and exported functions, but not this one. `omarchy-update-stay-awake` already honours it, but there it guards no user code. A standalone run with the variable set and an existing ticket issues no `sudo -k` at all. Setting it already requires running as the user, so this part is low severity.

**Suggested change:** use a channel-specific variable passed only on the refresh call from `omarchy-channel-set`, instead of exporting the update's flag for the whole switch. That fixes the overlap with `omarchy update`; any caller could still set a channel-only variable, which is the low-severity part above. Alternatively, keep the shared flag and update `docs/update-process.md:156`. `channel_sudo_session` (`bin/omarchy-refresh-pacman:23,25`) is set but never read.

### Dev path asks for the password before cloning and validating the checkout

`authorize_channel` (`bin/omarchy-channel-set:172`) now runs before `link_dev_checkout`, which clones `~/omarchy` if needed and then checks the required files. In the mock run with a stale checkout, b19dfb1 prompts for the password and then fails with "Update the checkout before switching to dev…". 3faafba rejected it with no prompt. The existing test "a stale dev checkout is rejected before linking or privileged work" still passes, because its check looks for `sudo -N` calls and dev-link/state steps, not the direct `sudo /usr/bin/true`. A fresh `git clone` also now runs while the ticket is live. Git runs a post-checkout hook after a clone, which can come from the user's template directory or `core.hooksPath`; this was taken from git's documentation and not executed.

**Impact:** a user with an outdated `~/omarchy` enters a password for a switch that is then rejected, and the existing stale-checkout test does not detect the new prompt. On a fresh clone, any post-checkout hook from the user's git configuration runs while the ticket is live.

**Suggested change:** clone and validate the checkout first (no sudo needed), then call `authorize_channel` just before `omarchy-dev-link`.

**Optional test improvement:** these mutants still pass all 19 checks in `channel-sudo-boundary-test.sh`:
- Removing `end_channel_authorization || exit 1` before the hand-off still passes. The "revokes before the update starts" assertion is satisfied by `omarchy-update`'s own entry `sudo -k` (`bin/omarchy-update:28`), which is logged before `step:omarchy-update-lock`.
- Removing `trap cleanup_channel EXIT`, or the kill and wait in `end_channel_authorization`, also passes. Nothing observes the keepalive, whose 60 s sleep never elapses in a test run.

The HUP/INT/TERM and failure blocks the PR body lists are unchanged from 3faafba. They now run through `cleanup_channel` but still check only the end state (no ticket, a final revocation, post-update not reached), not the keepalive.

**Coordination:** open #13444 changes the same `omarchy-update -y` hand-off line that this PR inserts the revocation above. Whichever merges second needs a small manual resolution that keeps both changes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of b19dfb1 against quattro 3faafba, plus sandboxed runs of the seven repository shell test files that exercise the changed scripts and of diagnostic scenarios on both revisions. Sudo was always a mock: the repository's own in its tests, and one modelled on sudo 1.9.17p2 source (`check.c`, `timestamp.c`, `parse_args.c`) in the diagnostic runs. No real sudo, pacman or channel switch ran. Prompt counts assume default sudoers (tty tickets). With `timestamp_type=ppid` or `timestamp_timeout=0`, the shared ticket may not reach child sudo calls; this was inferred from source and not tested. Merge conflicts with other open PRs were checked by text merge only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
